images.text: Heng O, the beautiful sister of a water god, was married to Sheng Yi, an accomplished archer. One day, Heng O was astonished to discover that her husband had been given a magic potion by one of the gods. She found the container of potion when she was cleaning the house. A very special power was contained in the potion – the power of immortality. On the spur of the moment, when Sheng Yi was out hunting one day, Heng O drank the potion. The full power of the potion was not known to her. In an instant, she was made weightless and flew out of the window.

When Sheng Yi returned home, he looked up to the sky and saw his wife floating up towards the moon. As quick as a flash, he knew what she had done. He tried to follow her, but a huge storm came up out of nowhere and Sheng Yi was lifted to the palace of the god of the immortals. It was this god who gave Sheng Yi another gift. It was the sun, where he would make his new home.

Heng O has lived on the moon ever since, in a beautiful palace made of precious stones. For many, many years, on the fifteenth day of every month, her husband has flown from the sun to visit his wife and brings rays of light with him to the moon. Some say that he is still angry with her for stealing the potion of immortality, so angry that he changed her into a three-legged frog. He wanted her to think about what she had done. If you look carefully on a clear night, you can see Heng O's frog shape in the moon.

The Simple Past Tense: Active and Passive Forms

The Simple Past tense refers to a finished action that happened at a definite time in the past.

You can use this tense in two ways: in an active structure and in a passive structure.
Let's look at how the structure changes when you talk about the past in an active voice and in then in a passive voice.

She wrapped a package ---> A package was wrapped by her.
They loved their children ---> Their children were loved by them.

She did not hear about the concert.----> Nothing about the concert was heard by her.
He did not pass on any gossip. ----> Gossip was not passed on by him.

In an interrogative sentence the active form begins with did. When a question in the active form starts with a question word, the passive sentence will as well. When a question in the active form starts with who or whose, the passive sentence will start with by whom or by whose.

Did he break the TV? ---> Was the TV broken by him?
Who killed the spider? ----> By whom was the spider killed?
Why did she fire you? ----> Why were you fired by her?
You use the passive structure when you want to shift the focus from the doer of the action to the receiver.
He tried to follow her, but a huge storm came up out of nowhere.
He looked up to the sky and saw his wife floating up towards the moon.
Sheng Yi was lifted to the palace of the god of the immortals.
A very special power was contained in the potion.
The full power of the potion was not known to her.
In an instant, she was made weightless.
The Simple Past and Present Perfect Tenses
What is the difference between the Simple Past and Present Perfect tenses?
You use the Simple Past tense to talk about finished events that have no connection to the present.
You use the Present Perfect for actions which started in the past and are still happening now OR for finished actions which have a connection to the present.

You don't use the Present Perfect tense with a finished time word:
NOT: I've been to the cafe yesterday.
